main_text.head: CHARACTE-RUM IESUITI-CORUM CENTURIA QUARTA, ex D. Augustini scriptis Polemicis collecta,
main_text.p: Si quid tēporalis molestiæ passi fuerint [ut de persecutione Anglicana tragicis & famosis libellis passim hodie conqueruntur Iesuitæ] per certissimum atq; rectissimum ordinem potestatum, cùm ipsis priuatis furiosorum agminibus multa grauiora passim atq; quotidie, nulla regia, nulla Ecclesiastica lege committant: nos corporum persecutores vocant, sc animarum interfectores non vocant, cùm priuata licentia corporibus parcant. Sed quia semper per mansuetudinem Christianam multò seuerius oculus iudicatur cuiusus[?] in lite, quàm animus excæcatus in schismate, & aduersum nos loquuntur, & nobiscum loquuntur: & cùm eos obmutescere compellat veritas, silere non permittit iniquitas. lib. 1. contra Epistolam Parmeniani.
Tanto isti amore hominum cæci sunt, & corde

page.notes: Two small "(" marks stand in the left margin beside the first paragraph; they are printer's marks or stray marks, not text, and were not transcribed. The word "cuiusus" (line 9 of paragraph I) is doubtful; it may be "cuiusuis" with a worn letter. The abbreviation over "temporalis" is read as a macron and may be a tilde. The page ends mid-sentence ("& corde"), and the sentence continues on the next page. No catchword is visible.
